Incorporating SLOOS alongside the Dec 14, 2022 FOMC action and the FSR shifts the read more negative than a policy-only lens:

- Policy: Hawkish hike to 4.25–4.50% with guidance for “ongoing increases,” higher IORB (4.4%) and ON RRP (4.3%), and continued QT—tightening financial conditions.
- FSR backdrop: Fragile market liquidity, elevated rate volatility, rising term premia, and vulnerabilities in NBFIs/MMFs heighten transmission risks to growth and risk assets.
- SLOOS confirmation of tightening credit supply:
  - Banks reported tightening across C&I and CRE (including construction/land development, nonfarm nonresidential, and multifamily).
  - Residential real estate standards tighter (subprime, non-QM jumbo, and QM jumbo); broader consumer credit standards tighter (notably credit cards).
  - Approval standards tougher for lower FICO (620/680), more favorable only for 720.
  - Foreign banks also tightened C&I, reinforcing global credit restraint.
- SLOOS demand signals:
  - Weaker loan demand from large, middle-market, and small firms; weaker demand for credit card and auto loans; overall consumer loan demand mixed/unchanged, with stronger HELOC demand.
- Banks cite economic outlook and recession risk as reasons for tightening; many assess elevated recession likelihood.

Net effect: SLOOS indicates the Fed’s tightening is transmitting forcefully via bank lending, amplifying downside growth risks beyond the FSR-based assessment. Adjusting the prior slightly negative score downward to reflect tighter credit supply and weaker demand.
